project.objective: Did Rafael Reyes and his wife Serapia Benavides Cueva of Usulután, El Salvador have a daughter named Rita, born and died in 1913?

questions.question: Does a birth registration for a daughter named Rita appear in Usulután, El Salvador civil records for 1913, listing Rafael Reyes and Serapia Benavides Cueva as parents?
questions.rationale: The objective asks whether this couple had a daughter Rita born and died in 1913. The birth registration is the gatekeeper fact: El Salvador implemented civil registration in 1879, so 1913 records should exist. Usulután departmental civil registry books are the most direct source. Confirming the birth establishes the child's existence before the death question can be meaningfully pursued.

The FamilySearch index 'birth: January 1913' was a data-entry error duplicating the death date. No 1913 birth registration exists because Rita was not born in 1913. Remaining plan items (pli_002–pli_005) skipped as premised on an infant 1913 birth that the original image disproves.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Rita Reyes as Daughter of Manuel Rafael Reyes and Serapia Benavides Cueva

**Research question:** Does a birth registration for a daughter named Rita appear in Usulután, El Salvador civil records for 1913, listing Rafael Reyes and Serapia Benavides Cueva as parents?

**Tier:** Probable | **Form:** Summary

### Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that Rita Reyes, who died in January 1913 in Santa Elena, Usulután, El Salvador, was the legitimate daughter of Manuel Rafael Reyes (known as Rafael Reyes, MTNY-RXQ) and Serapia Benavides Cueva (MTNY-RFX). No birth registration for a 1913-born infant named Rita exists in the searched records because Rita was an adult woman at the time of her death — not a newborn. The question's infant-birth premise is refuted by the original register image; however, the underlying objective — confirming Rita's existence and parentage — is answered affirmatively at the probable tier.

### Documented Negative: No 1913 Birth Registration

Four searches of the FamilySearch El Salvador Civil Registration collection (collection 1821208, "El Salvador Registro Civil, 1704-2001"), using query variants targeting 'Rita Reyes' in Usulután with various name forms, isPrincipal filters, and date parameters, returned no birth registration for a daughter named Rita born to this couple in 1913. The FamilySearch index entry that prompted this question displayed 'birth: January 1913' for a Rita Reyes in this collection — but examination of the original register page confirmed this was a data-entry error: the indexer duplicated the death month and year (January 1913) into the birth date field. The original Parte N°75 records no birth date for Rita whatsoever.

### The Civil Death Registration (Parte N°75)

The record found is a civil death registration (reposición de defunción), Parte N°75, entered at the Alcaldía Municipal of Santa Elena, Usulután, on 22 July 1932 — nineteen years after the underlying events. The registration was executed pursuant to a sentencia ejecutoriada (court judgment) issued by Judge Marco Antonio Ochoa, Juzgado Primero de Primera Instancia, Usulután, with registrar Miguel Ángel Velásques signing and secretary Carlos Aparicio Florencio Herrera countersigning.

The original register text (transcribed from image ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9TRR-4T4) reads in relevant part:

> "la señora Rita Reyes, quien fué soltera, de oficios domésticos y de este domicilio, hija legítima de Manuel Rafael Reyes y Serapia Benavides, falleció de parto en el mes de Enero de año mil novecientos trece en esta villa y que fué sepultada en el Cementerio de esta misma…"

Translation: 'the señora Rita Reyes, who was single, of domestic occupations and of this domicile, legitimate daughter of Manuel Rafael Reyes and Serapia Benavides, died in childbirth in the month of January of the year nineteen thirteen in this town and was buried in the Cemetery of this same [municipality]…'

This register establishes four facts bearing on the research question: (1) **Rita's adult status** — she is addressed as 'la señora' and carries an occupation (oficios domésticos) and marital status (soltera), attributes that would not appear for an infant, conclusively refuting the infant-birth premise; (2) **cause of death** — de parto (in childbirth), confirming she died as an adult woman in labor; (3) **parentage** — she is recorded as 'hija legítima' (legitimate daughter) of 'Manuel Rafael Reyes y Serapia Benavides,' directly answering the parentage question; (4) **place and approximate date of death** — Santa Elena, Usulután, January 1913.

### Source Classification and Reliability

**Source:** "El Salvador Registro Civil, 1704-2001," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6DQ4-1RQC : accessed 4 August 2026), entry for Rita Reyes and Manuel Rafael Reyes, 22 July 1932.

**Three-layer GPS classification:**
- *Source type:* **Original** — the original civil register page (image ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9TRR-4T4) was examined and transcribed, superseding the derivative FamilySearch index.
- *Information quality:* **Primary** for the registration act itself (the registrar personally recorded the 22 July 1932 proceedings). **Secondary** for the underlying biographical facts — Rita's death in January 1913, her parentage, occupation, and marital status — because this information was supplied through court proceedings nineteen years after the events, by informants whose identity is not specified in the record.
- *Evidence type:* **Direct** — the record explicitly names Rita as 'hija legítima de Manuel Rafael Reyes y Serapia Benavides,' directly answering the parentage question without requiring inference.

The nineteen-year gap between the 1913 death and the 1932 registration is a reliability concern: informants' recollections over such a span may be imperfect. The court-judgment mechanism (sentencia ejecutoriada) partially mitigates this risk, as the court was required to weigh evidence before certifying the facts — providing institutional scrutiny absent from a simple declarant registration. Nevertheless, the secondary classification of the biographical facts is warranted.

### Index Error: Resolved

The only discrepancy identified — the FamilySearch index showing 'birth: January 1913' for Rita Reyes — has been explained and superseded. The original register image contains no birth date for Rita; the indexer duplicated the death date into the birth field. Assertion a_003 capturing this erroneous indexed birth date has been marked superseded and is excluded from this conclusion. No unresolved conflicts remain.

### Identity Links

- **Rita Reyes (I1):** The record uniquely identifies the deceased as 'la señora Rita Reyes,' soltera, oficios domésticos, resident of Santa Elena, Usulután, hija legítima of Manuel Rafael Reyes and Serapia Benavides, buried in Santa Elena's municipal cemetery. I1 is a new tree person grounded in this single record.
- **Manuel Rafael Reyes / Rafael Reyes (MTNY-RXQ):** The father named as 'Manuel Rafael Reyes' is linked at probable confidence to tree person MTNY-RXQ (Rafael Reyes). In Spanish naming practice, 'Manuel Rafael' designates a person whose baptismal first name is Manuel and whose commonly used name is Rafael; the surname Reyes and the Usulután family context align with no identified conflict.
- **Serapia Benavides Cueva (MTNY-RFX):** The mother named as 'Serapia Benavides' is linked at confident confidence to MTNY-RFX. The given name Serapia is highly distinctive and matches exactly; the primary surname Benavides matches exactly; the maternal surname Cueva is commonly omitted in civil registers and its absence is typical rather than discrepant.

### Limitations

Only one source was located. GPS Component 1 (reasonably exhaustive research) was declared exhaustive for this question's literal scope, but the absence of independent corroboration caps the conclusion at the probable tier. A Catholic baptismal record for Rita — whose birth year remains unestablished by this evidence — or a contemporaneous civil record from Santa Elena naming her parents could independently verify the parentage without being expected to overturn it. Rita's birth year is not established by any evidence gathered; that determination would require a separate research question targeting baptismal or civil birth records across the years before 1913.

### Conclusion Statement

The evidence strongly suggests that Rita Reyes, an adult woman who died in childbirth in January 1913 in Santa Elena, Usulután, El Salvador, was the legitimate daughter of Manuel Rafael Reyes (Rafael Reyes, MTNY-RXQ) and Serapia Benavides Cueva (MTNY-RFX). The preponderance of direct evidence from an original civil register — executed through a court judgment nineteen years after the events — supports this parentage at the probable tier. No birth registration for a 1913-born infant named Rita exists; the research question's infant-birth premise is refuted. The couple did have a daughter named Rita who died in January 1913 as an adult woman.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Usulután, El Salvador (1900–1920)

## Jurisdiction
Usulután is both a **department** (created 1865) and a **municipality** within that department in eastern El Salvador. Civil records for this period were created at the municipal level and are held/digitized by FamilySearch primarily through the *El Salvador, Civil Registration, 1704-2001* collection.

## Civil Registration (Primary Source)
**Collection:** El Salvador, Civil Registration, 1704-2001 (FS collection 1821208; 3,150,368 records, 1,381,210 images). Also mirrored on Ancestry (collection 9838) and MyHeritage.
- Covers births (nacimientos), deaths (defunciones), and marriages (matrimonios).
- El Salvador mandated civil registration from 1879; this is the primary record type for 1913.
- **Critical gap:** Volume-level browse shows no discrete 1910–1914 birth or death volumes for Usulután municipality. However, the main collection index covers the broad date range (1704–2023) and should surface 1913 records when searched by name. Search the collection directly before concluding records are absent.
- Discrete Usulután birth volumes confirmed: 1886–1902 (100% indexed), 1903–1909 (44–97% indexed), 1915–1916 (100% indexed), 1917–1920 (77–97% indexed).
- Discrete Usulután death volumes confirmed: 1915–1917, 1918–1920, 1919–1980 — no discrete 1913 death volume found.
- **Access:** Indexed (name-searchable) via FamilySearch.org at collection 1821208; most volumes also have images.

## Catholic Church / Sacramental Records (Secondary Source)
**Collection:** El Salvador, Catholic Church Records, 1655–1977 (FS collection 1919582; 3,169,964 records). Also: El Salvador, Baptisms, 1750–1940 (FS collection 1584970; 145,495 records).
- **Santa Catarina de Alejandría parish** (Usulután municipality, Usulután department) has baptismal volumes:
  - 1894–1913 (volumes 15–19): 96–99% name-indexed, full-text searchable — covers exactly through 1913.
  - 1914–1924 (volumes 20–21): 89–97% name-indexed.
  - Religious death records: 1875–1940 (volumes 1–4): 92–95% name-indexed.
- Church baptismal registers recorded godparents and parents' names; very useful if the civil birth registration is absent.
- All records are in Spanish.

## Late Registration (Reposiciones)
- Reposiciones de nacimientos volumes for Usulután municipality cover 1916–1919 (full-text searchable). These are late or corrected registrations and may document births originally unregistered in 1913.
